monument_name: Rārā Temple and fountain (14th-15th cent. CE)
description_en: Theśikharatemple and fountain (dhārāormugrāhā) is located on the northern side of Rārā lake, next to a track.Theśikharatemple (MUG0100-001) has little dimensions; thesanctumis 40 x 43 cm. Its content could not be assessed as the monument is partially buried. It is therefore unknown if the sanctum contains aliṅgaor not. From the current level around it, the temple is 155 cm high. Including the burried part, the approximate height must be around 185 cm. The temple is oriented to the south, towards the fontain.The fountain (MUG0100-002) is found 60 cm south of the temple. The stone facing contains carved elements with pilasters moulded plinths. The fountain originally had two spouts. Only one is left. It is carved in the shape of amakara. Stone slabs are arranged on the eastern and western sides of the fountain so as to make steps to access water. The monument is half buried.The plan with a combination of aśikharatemple and a fountain is locally known asdevaldhārā.This type of construction was probably introduced from Uttarakhand (Chanchani 2019, 19). In west Nepal this type of plan is only met in the Jumla district and it has one occurence in the Dailekh and Mugu districts (Andolfatto 2019, 79-93). This geographic repartition may indicate a regional preference that could politicaly correspond to the Kalyāla dynasty of Jumla. This would date the site from c. 14th-15th century.
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019. Chanchani, Nachiket. Mountain Temples and Temple Mountains. Architecture, Religion, and Nature in the Central Himalayas . Seattle: University of Washington Press, 2019.
